c7W8jpsjtCc_better_hook_v1.angle: xAI’s Grok 4.6 looks less like a benchmark win and more like a shift toward reliable long-running agent work.
c7W8jpsjtCc_better_hook_v1.post_text:
xAI's Grok 4.6 looks like a real step forward, but the bigger story is why it matters.

It seems better at longer agent tasks. It stays on task more reliably, works with sub-agents more naturally, and handles multi-step work without drifting as much. That matters because the real question is no longer just whether a model can answer a prompt. The question is whether it can actually finish the job.

There is still a tradeoff. Grok 4.6 appears stronger than 4.5 in real use, but it also seems less efficient with tokens, which can make it slower and more expensive. That is the hard balance frontier labs keep running into: better intelligence is useful, but only if the cost and speed stay practical.

My takeaway: xAI is closing the gap, and the competition is shifting toward reliability on real tasks, not just benchmark scores.

#AI #LLMs #Agents #CodingAI #xAI

434cG4g5KLE_builder_insight_v1.angle: Use AI-generated disposable verification code to protect the smaller set of code that actually ships.
434cG4g5KLE_builder_insight_v1.post_text:
AI-generated code changes the review problem.

The easy reaction is to ask engineers to read faster. I don’t think that is the useful lesson.

The better move is to split generated code into two categories: code that ships, and code that helps you decide what deserves to ship.

The first category still needs care. If a change touches production, security, money, infrastructure, or anything users depend on, it belongs in the normal review path.

The second category is where AI gets really interesting.

Generate the test harness. Generate the one-off debugger. Generate the custom lint rule. Generate the API probe, stress test, compiler hook, or tiny script that answers one question and can be thrown away afterwards.

That kind of code does not need to be precious. It needs to increase confidence.

So the practical shift is not “merge more AI code.”

It is: use more disposable code to protect the small amount of code that actually matters.

That is a much stronger operating model for AI-assisted engineering.

#AIEngineering #SoftwareEngineering #DeveloperTools #CodeReview #Testing
